title: FAST: An Optimization Framework for Fast Additive Segmentation in Transparent ML

problem.claim: Fitting transparent additive models with piecewise constant shape functions can be computationally slow.

gap.claim: Existing state-of-the-art methods do not provide sufficiently fast optimization for additive segmentation.

contributions.claim: FAST is an optimization framework for fast additive segmentation that fits transparent additive models by segmenting piecewise constant shape functions for each feature.
FAST includes feature selection algorithms for fitting parsimonious additive models.

stated_novelty.claim: The framework introduces a novel optimization procedure and new feature selection algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the optimization procedure fits additive models approximately two orders of magnitude faster than existing state-of-the-art methods such as explainable boosting machines.
Through experiments and case studies, the authors report improved computational efficiency and interpretability of additive models.
The authors report that the feature selection algorithms produce parsimonious models that perform well.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces FAST as an optimization framework for fast additive segmentation.
Describes piecewise constant shape-function segmentation, a novel optimization procedure, and feature selection algorithms for parsimonious models.
Reports speed, computational-efficiency, interpretability, and model-performance improvements based on experiments and case studies.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines faster optimization with feature selection for parsimonious additive models.

interpretation.claim: Transparent-model methods may benefit from jointly addressing computational cost and model complexity.

application.claim: When developing interpretable additive models, consider pairing optimization improvements with feature-selection mechanisms.
